# ap - Agent Instructions

`ap` (short for **autoproject**) is an opinionated automation tool for gke-labs projects. It uses a "convention over configuration" approach to handle common development tasks.

## Repository Root and Subtrees

- The git repository root (containing `.git`) is the only root; configuration is read from `<repo>/.ap/`.
- Commands operate on a subtree of the repository: either the positional target when specified (e.g., `ap e2e autodeploy`, `ap deploy <dir>`), the subtree of the current working directory, or the whole repository when run from the root.
- Subtree overrides: A `.ap/` directory in a subtree can override configuration options for files beneath it. The effective configuration for a path is the base configuration with keys overridden by the nearest enclosing subtree `.ap/go.yaml`, walking up to the root (only present keys override, absent keys inherit, lists such as `skip` replace, explicitly written keys win, mapping sections merge per key). Overrides apply to `gofmt`, `govet`, `govulncheck`, `tidy`, `skip`, `lint` (analyzer modes and baselines), and `toolchain`, while tool version files (`protoc.yaml`, `docker.yaml`, `kind.yaml`, `kubectl.yaml`, `kustomize.yaml`) and `.ap/ap.yaml` remain root-only. Subtree `.ap/` directories do not change discovery, build context, image naming, or generated presubmits. Example subtree `.ap/go.yaml`:
  ```yaml
  govulncheck:
    enabled: false
  ```

## Initializing / Onboarding Projects

To onboard a repository or subdirectory onto `ap`, run `ap init`:

```bash
go run github.com/gke-labs/gke-labs-infra/ap@latest init --copyright-holder "<Organization>"
```

- Creates `.ap/` with starter `ap.yaml` (`version: latest`), `go.yaml`, and `headers.yaml`.
- Pass `--license none` to disable license header checks, or `--license apache-2.0` (default).
- Pass `--generate` to initialize and generate CI presubmits in one step:

```bash
go run github.com/gke-labs/gke-labs-infra/ap@latest init --copyright-holder "<Organization>" --generate
```

## Recommended Workflow for Agents

When making changes to an AP-managed project, coding agents should follow this verification sequence:

0.  **Initialize (if onboarding)**: If the repository or component is not yet configured for `ap`, run `ap init`.
1.  **Generate Code**: Run `ap generate` to update any generated files, CI scripts, or manifests (note: `ap generate` also runs `ap fmt` to format code, tidy Go modules, and stamp license headers).
2.  **Lint**: Run `ap lint` to ensure code follows project style and quality guidelines.
    -   When adopting a strict check at `mode: error` with existing findings, run `ap lint --write-baseline`, commit the `.ap/*-baseline.txt` files, and fix entries over time.
    -   Task scripts must be portable across macOS and Linux; `ap lint` flags known GNU-only / bash-4-only constructs.
3.  **Test**:
    -   Run `ap test` for unit and integration tests.
    -   Run `ap e2e` for end-to-end tests.
        -   If a root has `tests/e2e` Go tests, `ap e2e` runs `RUN_E2E=1 go test -v -count=1 -timeout 30m ./tests/e2e/...`. A `dev/tasks/test-e2e*` script at the same root runs before them and is for setup only (build a binary, prepare a cluster, free disk space); it must not run the Go tests itself, or they run twice.
        -   If a kind worker's kubelet restarts in a loop while other nodes are Ready, check inotify limits; CI jobs that create more than one kind cluster should raise them with a visible `sudo sysctl -w` step.

## Deployment

-   **Command**: `ap deploy`
-   **Targets**: Positional arguments select targets: `ap deploy <dir>` applies every manifest under any `k8s/` directory beneath `<dir>`, `ap deploy <dir>/k8s/<file>.yaml` applies a single file and builds only images that file references, and `ap deploy <dir>/kustomization.yaml` (or `ap deploy <dir>` where `<dir>` contains `kustomization.yaml`) builds with `kustomize build` and applies the generated YAML as a manifest with ApplySet support.
-   **Images**: `ap` automatically builds Docker images found in the `images/<image-name>` directory. Built images deployed with `:latest` are pinned by digest (`tag@sha256`) in applied manifests so redeploying always rolls pods to the new image.
-   **Kubernetes**: `ap` deploys Kubernetes manifests located in the `k8s` directory.
-   **Kind**: When the current context is a kind cluster, `ap deploy` works with no `IMAGE_PREFIX`, building locally, loading images into the kind cluster using a unique tag, and applying.
-   **Cluster**: Use `--cluster=kind://<name>` to target a specific kind cluster or `--cluster=<context>` to target a kubeconfig context.
-   **Namespace**: Passing `-n <namespace>` retargets namespaced objects to the target namespace while logging changes and applying cluster-scoped objects as-is.
-   **ApplySet**: Pass `--applyset=[RESOURCE[.GROUP]/]NAME` to track deployments with KEP-3659 ApplySet labels and maintain parent metadata.
-   **BuildKit**: Configure remote BuildKit using `--buildkit-host` or `BUILDKIT_HOST` (e.g. `k8s://namespace/service`); the `k8s` shorthand expands to `k8s://autodeploy-system/buildkit`.
-   **Buildctl**: The buildkit path uses the pinned `buildctl`.
-   **Registry Prefix**: `IMAGE_PREFIX` defaults to `images.local`, assuming an in-cluster image registry and its node agent.
-   **Skip Push**: Use `--skip-push` to skip pushing built images to the registry.
-   **Manifest Scope**: Manifests are applied as written apart from image references and namespace retargeting; `ap deploy` does not install missing CRDs or create Secrets.

## Tool Management

- `ap tool install [dir]` creates symlinks for managed tools (`kind`, `kubectl`, `kustomize`, `docker`, `docker-buildx`, `protoc`, `go`) pointing to `ap` for busybox-style dispatch to pinned tool binaries. In a repository, it defaults to `${REPO_ROOT}/.build/bin`. Discovered task scripts have `${REPO_ROOT}/.build/bin` prepended to `PATH` automatically. Scripts should call tools by name and never download them; `ap` provides them on `PATH`.
- `ap bash <script> [args...]` runs a bash script from the repository root with `${REPO_ROOT}/.build/bin` on `PATH` and `REPO_ROOT` exported (`#!/usr/bin/env -S ap bash`, requires coreutils 8.30+).
    -   Scripts should assume bash 4+, and `ap bash` warns when the local bash is older.

## Kubernetes Manifests

When writing Kubernetes manifests, follow these guidelines:

-   **Do not specify `imagePullPolicy`**: Kubernetes will automatically set a reasonable default (e.g., `Always` if the tag is `:latest`, `IfNotPresent` otherwise).
-   **Image Naming**: The image name should map to the directory name under `images`. For example, a Dockerfile at `images/foo/Dockerfile` will result in an image named `${IMAGE_PREFIX}/foo`. In your manifest, you should specify the image as `foo` or `foo:latest`. `ap` will handle the prefixing during deployment.

## Task Output

Every leaf task runs with buffered output, printing a status line per task (`=== <name> (ok|FAILED, <duration>)`) and emitting captured output only on failure (pass `-v=1` to print output for passing tasks). `ap e2e` prints leaf task output at default verbosity so test execution results are visible in CI job logs. When `$ARTIFACTS` is set, every leaf task writes its buffered output to `$ARTIFACTS/tasks/<task-name>.log` whether it passed or failed. Tasks obtain a `logr.Logger` via `tc.Log()` or `scoped.Log(ctx)` that writes directly into this buffer using structured key/value pairs (warnings logged with `"level", "warning"`). Built images log a summary line (`built <image> with <builder> in <duration>; sent <bytes>`), where buildctl reports context bytes sent and Docker omits bytes because buildx does not expose them.
